function.name: Music_3_PlayMedia
function.description: Plays a specified track on a designated media player device. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

track.description: The title of the song to be played.

function.name: Music_3_LookupMusic
function.description: Retrieve a list of songs that align with the user's musical preferences based on artist, album, genre, and release year. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

artist.description: The name of the artist or band. Use 'dontcare' if this is not a filtering criterion.

album.description: The title of the album. Use 'dontcare' if this is not a filtering criterion.

genre.description: The musical genre of the songs. Select 'dontcare' to include all genres.

year.description: The release year of the song. Use 'dontcare' to include songs from any year.

message.reasoning:
The user says they want to listen to some music; specifically Imagine Dragons and mentions an album called Night Visions (which is actually their debut studio album). They likely want to play it.

We have two relevant functions:

1) Music_3_PlayMedia - plays a specified track on a designated media player device. We can specify track, artist, etc. But we don't know which track exactly. Maybe they'd like to play the entire album? There's no direct function to stream an album. However, maybe we could use PlayMedia specifying track=some track from Night Visions. Or we might need to look up tracks first using LookupMusic then pick one.

But the request: "listen to some music, imagine dragons would be awesome, somebody told me about the night visions album". So perhaps we should ask them what track they'd like to hear from that album. Alternatively, we could just start playing something from that album. Let's propose a popular track e.g., "Radioactive".

Thus call Music_3_PlayMedia with track="Radioactive", artist="Imagine Dragons", device default living room.

Let's do that.
